verses.1: On those days, there were still many people who were hungry and didn’t know what to eat. He invited the disciples and said to them:
verses.2: I’m worried about the crowd, as three days have already passed, and they still don’t know what to do.
verses.3: And if I dismiss them as guests in their own homes, they will still be welcome along the way. And some of them will even come from far away.
verses.4: And his disciples said to him, “How can anyone carry these people across the desert on their backs?”
verses.5: And he asked them, “How many potatoes do you have?” They replied, “Seven.”
verses.6: And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then, after taking the seven loaves, he thanked God and handed them to his disciples, so that they could give them to the crowd. And they did so.
verses.7: And they had only a little fish. When he thanked them for it, he also said that these should be given away as well.
verses.8: And they ate and were satisfied. They also received extra portions of seven types of food.
verses.9: They were, in fact, forty-six in number. And he dismissed them.
verses.10: And immediately, he entered the ship along with his disciples. Then he arrived in the regions of Dalmanutha.
verses.11: And the Pharisees came and began to discuss with him, asking him for a sign from heaven, trying to test him.
verses.12: And he said to his spirit, “What kind of destiny is this that demands a sign? Indeed, I tell you, if a sign is given to this family, then it will be so.”
verses.13: And after they were sent away again, he went back to the other side.
verses.14: And they were also unable to get any bread to eat; they didn’t have any bread with them on the ship at all.
verses.15: And he instructed them, “Look! See the bondage of the Pharisees, and also the bondage of Herodes.”
verses.16: And they argued with each other that they didn’t have any vegetables.
verses.17: And God says to them, “Why do you argue that you have no bread? Don’t you understand that you also won’t be able to eat? Your hearts are filled with sorrow.”
verses.18: Having eyes, yet you cannot see; having ears, yet you cannot hear. And you do not remember either.
verses.19: When I divided the five fruits among the fifty thousand people, how many coptes of grain did they fill each person with? They said to him: Twelve.
verses.20: And those seven, out of the forty thousand, how many payments in coins did they receive? They said to him, “Seven.”
verses.21: And he said to them, “Do you really want to go?”
verses.22: And they go to Bethsaida. They bring him a blind man, and they ask him to touch him.
verses.23: And taking the blind man’s hand, he led him out of the city. Then, putting his hands on the blind man’s eyes, he tried to see what was happening around him. “Can you see anything?”
verses.24: And when you looked at them, he said, “I see these people as trees that are moving around.”
verses.25: Then, once again, he placed his hands over his eyes. He looked away, and then stared at everything around him in the dark.
verses.26: And he sent him to his house, saying, “Do not go into the city.”
verses.27: And Jesus and His disciples went to the courts of Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples, saying, “What will people say about me?”
verses.28: But those who said to him that John the Baptist was it, and others said Elijah; yet others said that he was one of the prophets.
verses.29: And he also questioned them. “What do you call me?” Peter replied, “You are the Christ.”
verses.30: And he ordered that they should not say anything about him to anyone.
verses.31: And he began to teach them that a human son must suffer many hardships and be subjected to the oppression of elders, high priests, and officials. He also said that after three days, he would rise again.
verses.32: And with ease, he understood the words. Then, when Peter hired him, he began to praise him.
verses.33: And when he returned and saw his disciples, he praised Peter and said, “Come back to me, Satan! You do not care about what God wants, but only what humans want.”
verses.34: And when he called together the crowd along with his disciples, he said to them, “If anyone wants to return to me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.”
verses.35: For those who wish to save their souls, they must first destroy them themselves. But those who do destroy their own souls, they will still be saved by me and by the gospel.
verses.36: What good does it do for a person to gain the whole world, if in doing so he has to suffer greatly in his soul?
verses.37: What can a person give in exchange for his soul?
verses.38: For if he deceives me, along with those who speak against me in this same deceitful and wicked way, then the son of man will also be deceived when he comes in the glory of his father with the angels of holiness.
